questions.question: A pharmacy phone agent mishears two drug names, but only these two words fail. You need the fastest fix with no data collection or training. What should you do?

options.why: This works but needs data and training.

options.text: Add a phrase list that contains the two drug names
options.why: Correct. A phrase list boosts specific words with no training.

options.text: Switch to text to speech with SSML
options.why: Text to speech is output, and it does not affect recognition.
The error occurs before the model receives text.

questions.explanation: A phrase list is the quick fix for a few words. Train custom speech for many terms, accents or noisy audio.

questions.question: A call center has 3,000 product terms, regional accents and noisy lines. A phrase list does not improve recognition enough. What should you do?

options.text: Add more phrases to the list until it contains all terms
options.why: Phrase lists suit a small number of words.

options.text: Lower the speaking rate in SSML
options.why: SSML controls synthesis, not recognition.

options.text: Train and deploy a custom speech model and use its endpoint ID in the app
options.why: Correct. Custom speech uses your text and audio data for the domain.
Content Safety scores harm and does not improve recognition.

questions.explanation: Custom speech models are trained on related text or labelled audio, then called through a custom endpoint ID.

questions.question: Spoken replies from an agent read a time too fast: "your order is ready at five" is spoken in one breath. You must add a short pause and slow only the time. Which technique should you use?

options.text: Speech Synthesis Markup Language with a break element and a prosody rate
options.why: Correct. SSML controls pauses, rate, pitch and style.
Phrase lists apply to recognition.
Temperature changes the words generated, not the speaking.
Translation converts languages.

questions.explanation: SSML adds pauses and changes rate or pitch for text to speech output.

questions.question: You build a voice agent. The caller speaks, the agent answers and the reply is spoken. Which sequence describes one turn?

options.text: Text to speech, model, speech to text
options.why: The order is reversed.

options.text: Speech to text, model or agent, text to speech
options.why: Correct. Audio becomes text, the model answers, and the answer becomes audio.
This does not produce a spoken reply.

options.text: Model, speech to text, language detection
options.why: The model needs text before it answers.

questions.explanation: A basic voice loop is speech in, the model or agent, and speech out. Voice Live can run it as one low-latency connection.

questions.question: A phone agent needs low-latency speech in and speech out, noise suppression and turn detection, over a single connection with a model or an agent. Which feature should you use?

options.why: Batch transcription processes saved audio files, not live calls.
This scores harm in text.
This trains text translation models.
Correct. Voice Live runs real-time speech to speech with these built-in features.

questions.explanation: Voice Live provides a real-time speech interface for models and agents, including noise suppression and end-of-turn detection.
